description: Direct resolutions involving existing database principles, grouped by family; separately, questions about new principles, other negative results, and open problems. Recorded conjectures and their model variants remain exhaustively covered.

questions.question: Does Tame Rigidity + Rigid Power entail Weakly Rigid Power?
questions.status: Refuted by a certified full C countermodel
questions.established: No. The finite compression model satisfies Tame Rigidity and Rigid Power but fails Weakly Rigid Power at type et. The earlier colour-collapse example fails Rigid Power at the next property type and does not by itself settle this question.

questions.question: Does Relational Choice entail Transversal Choice?
questions.status: Unresolved; sharper positive and negative criteria
questions.established: Relational Choice plus Boolean Completeness gives Actuality and TC. The history construction reduces Transversal Choice at the evaluation point to finite ambiguity in at least one missed cell. Finite code orbits obstruct symmetry-based countermodels. Class-code iteration preserves ambiguity, and orbit exhaustion is exactly Actuality.
questions.remaining: Derive a suitable coherent chooser from RC alone, or construct a genuine full RC countermodel meeting the closure and code-orbit restrictions.

questions.question: Can Functional Choice or ☐Functional Choice have a finite equivalent fixed-type basis?
questions.established: Neither full Functional Choice nor its boxed form has an equivalent finite list of arbitrary pure fixed-type sentences over C. The Boolean-valued construction supplies ordinary separating models. The previously stated fixed-input and selector hierarchies remain in the supporting proofs.

questions.question: Can pure Maximalism coexist with Atomicity (type t)?
questions.established: The inconsistency theorem has no additional non-theoremhood or model-existence premise.

questions.question: Is pure Strong Possibility consistent?
questions.status: Unresolved; exact criteria and construction obstructions
questions.established: Universal-identity and restricted-disjunction criteria are established. In the specified two-axiom test any required full-term embedding must leave every target arithmetic counterexample above its entire source number image.
questions.remaining: Construct the genuine endpoint embedding or otherwise settle joint consistency. A noncofinal omitted-cut requirement rules out routes, not the theory.

questions.question: Is SP consistent for one unary predicate constant and no individual names?
questions.established: Nonempty K₁ already implies full signature SP consistency and is equivalent to weak named existence for the marked Max theory. Finite Herbrand extraction fails; the singleton-profile root is deleted. A successful fixed-domain kernel must be perfect and nonhyperarithmetic, with exact stabilization ordinal ω₁CK.
questions.remaining: Prove weak named existence or give a globally empty witness open. Failure of K₁ or the stronger fixed-domain construction would not alone refute SP.

questions.question: Can fixed C be reconstructed without primitive lambda?
questions.status: Exact open-sequent equivalence established and certified
questions.established: An explicit classical lambda-free applicative calculus has exactly C’s consequences in its original language, including open contexts and finite lists of assumptions. A conservative named extension reconstructs arbitrary C terms and full contextual beta eta delta conversion.

questions.question: Does injective logical separation imply logical left-inverse separation?
questions.status: Unresolved over H and over C5
questions.established:
Separation by logical observers with logical left inverses (SplitMono) entails separation by injective logical observers (InjSep). The converse asks whether a separating family can be replaced by one whose members have logical left inverses; it does not require each original observer to have such an inverse. Over C5, the exact decompositions are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{InjSep}&\longleftrightarrow\mathrm{Rev}\lor(\mathrm{OS}\land J_t),\\
\mathrm{SplitMono}&\longleftrightarrow\mathrm{Rev}\lor(\mathrm{OS}\land K_t).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $J_t$ says that some injective logical observer $E$ and currently true $c$ satisfy $\forall p(Ep\le c\to p=\bot)$. The condition $K_t$ says that logical observers $E,F$ and currently true $c$ satisfy $F\circ E=I$ and $Fc=\bot$. Both use the same qualification at type t; C5 reduces the full schemas to these finite instances. See the [injective](proofs/h-observer-space/injective-separation-decomposition.md) and [left-inverse](proofs/h-observer-space/left-inverse-separation-decomposition.md) decompositions.

The regular-open countermodel refutes $J_t\Rightarrow K_t$, but fails OS, so it does not settle the separation question. Finite relative generation gives a positive case. With $\mathrm{BC}_t+\mathrm{Zorn}_t$, the stated support-coverage equation supplies the required logical inverse; a currently true admitted homogeneous interval is another sufficient condition. The [theorem map](proofs/h-observer-space/MAP.md#10-explicit-frontier) records their exact premises.

The established hierarchy includes H + OS ⇒ C + BF and endpoint separation ⇔ C5 + Atomicity (type t). Reversible separation has an exact invariant-proposition characterization; the [group-law and finite-family theorems](proofs/h-observer-space/GRAPH.md#any-nontrivial-group-equation) give further exact regions without resolving this comparison.
questions.remaining:
The main C5 question is exactly whether

$$
\mathrm{C5}+\mathrm{OS}+J_t\ \vdash\ \mathrm{Rev}\lor K_t.
$$

Over H the corresponding question is InjSep ⇒ SplitMono. A countermodel must satisfy the full injective separation schema, rather than merely contain an injective observer lacking a logical left inverse.

Other unresolved comparisons are collected in the [research frontier](proofs/h-observer-space/MAP.md#10-explicit-frontier): the joint effect of $\mathrm{BC}_t$ and $\mathrm{Zorn}_t$ with OS; the remaining infinite connective and affine admission questions; the general atomless meet classification; the endpoint-parameter noncontingency converse for Rev; further inverse/necessity comparisons; and removing Actuality from the C-based FinBox theorem for empty or individual-only qualification lists.

questions.question: Can endpoint separation and comprehension reconstruct full standard models?
questions.status: Resolved: a λ-free characterization in ZF
questions.established: Full typed endpoint separation plus boxed Infinitary Comprehension characterizes full standard relational hierarchies over the specified λ-free base of H. Finite instances reconstruct abstraction, while the translated observer equality clauses follow from the resulting C5 theory. The representation is provable in ZF. [Proof and exact formulation](proofs/lambda-free-endpoint-comprehension.md).

questions.question: Does countable named exhaustion follow from SP with infinitary resources?
questions.status: Proved for a specified semantic reference; conditional otherwise
questions.established: A single admitted non-name predicate gives reflection. The profile construction supplies Max(Td)-eligibility, so SP(Td) entails countable actual exhaustion. A numeral abstraction conflicts with Max referenced to original finitary C.
questions.remaining: For a proposed syntactic C∞, supply the closed-identity separation bridge. Consistency of SP(Td) is not proved.

questions.question: Do ☐Rigid Comprehension, Intensional Choice and Forcing Possibilism force CH contingency?
questions.status: Strict-smallness database formulation refuted by existing models; source correspondence unresolved
questions.established:
No for the database’s strict-smallness formulation. Under metatheoretic Choice, countable-arrow full-action models satisfy all three premises together with Non-contingency of CH: the strict size bound requests only finite complete Boolean algebras in those models. This refutes the encoded conjecture; the source’s intended size convention and type language require separate comparison. See the [formulation audit](proofs/forcing-formulation.md).

Strict-smallness Forcing Possibilism is also independent over C + ☐Functional Choice + Axiom of Infinity (types e and t). The [full modalized cloud](evidence/RESULT-INDEX.md#forcing-transfer) has its own model-specific forcing-transfer argument.
questions.remaining: The stronger non-strict formulation and its required forcing-algebra availability remain unresolved. Equivalence of the two lottery presentations remains under review.

questions.question: Does strong profile richness force full Functional Choice?
questions.established: Supported nominal models realize exact individual profiles and arbitrarily high finite supported ranks while failing FC. Raw profile representation and rigid-profile PR have different boundaries.

questions.question: Does ☐Functional Choice add ordinary arithmetic over ☐Plenitude?
questions.established: Over C with quantified Infinity at e and t, replacing ☐Plenitude by ☐Functional Choice adds no ordinary first-order arithmetic theorems. Both have the arithmetic consequences of C plus numerical noncollapse at e, and this remains true after adding ☐Axiom of Infinity at every admitted type.
questions.remaining: The proof uses McLarty’s number-preserving interpretation.

questions.question: What exactly is the ordinary arithmetic theory of pure Maximalism?
questions.status: Proposed equality; upper inclusion awaits independent review
questions.established:
The proposed equality is

$$
\mathrm{Th}_{\mathrm{arith}}(\mathrm{Max}(C))=\mathrm{Cn}\bigl(T_{\mathrm{arith}}\cup\mathrm{True}_{\Pi_1}\bigr).
$$

An ordinary proof is supplied for both inclusions, but the difficult upper inclusion still awaits independent review. Here $T_{\mathrm{arith}}$ is the common arithmetic theory of the positive Choice and Plenitude packages. See the [statement and proof](evidence/RESULT-INDEX.md#max-arithmetic-equality).

questions.question: Does signature Strong Possibility entail pure Strong Possibility?
questions.status: Exact consistency reduction established; consistency remains unresolved
questions.established: For every map-admitted signature Σ, SP(Σ) entails SP(pure) exactly when SP(Σ) is inconsistent. More strongly, SP(pure) is incompatible with Max(Σ). The reverse entailment holds exactly when SP(pure) is inconsistent. The signature must contain a relational constant, and each Max schema retains its own reference language. See the [proof](evidence/RESULT-INDEX.md#sp-signature-conflict).
questions.remaining: This settles the relation between the two questions without deciding either consistency question.

formalization_status_source: MAIN-RESULTS.json; question statuses describe mathematical progress, independently of formalization.
title: Unresolved questions and resolved conjectures

database_questions.question: Does Actuality + BF imply Inextensible Comprehension?
database_questions.answer: Yes. BF need not be strengthened to ☐BF.
database_questions.contribution: **Existing database result:** Christopher Sun’s argument, written out by Claude Opus 5.5 at Cian Dorr’s prompting. The database already supplies the Lean formalization.

database_questions.question: Does Relational Choice + Boolean Completeness imply Transversal Choice?
database_questions.answer: Yes. The same premises also imply Actuality; Relational Choice alone remains open.
database_questions.contribution: **Contribution:** the RC + BC ⇒ Actuality proof and a direct proof of RC + BC ⇒ TC, with Lean formalization.

database_questions.question: Does ☐Atomicity + Boolean Completeness + BF imply Rigid Comprehension?
database_questions.answer: No. The ultralimit-fork model satisfies even ☐Boolean Completeness, ☐BF and ☐Actuality, but fails Rigid Comprehension at type tt.
database_questions.contribution: **Existing countermodel:** Branden Fitelson and collaborators, in Cian Dorr’s intensional action-model presentation. Included as a recorded resolution.

database_questions.question: Does Rigid Rigidity imply Rigid Power?
database_questions.answer: No. A coalesced sum of two extensional models disagreeing about arithmetic satisfies Rigid Rigidity and refutes Rigid Power.
database_questions.contribution: **Existing countermodel:** Cian Dorr’s coalesced construction, with verification by Claude Opus 5.5 and the rigidity verdicts by Claude Fable 5.1 at Dorr’s prompting.

database_questions.question: Does C5 + Atomicity imply No Pure Contingency?
database_questions.answer: Yes. Atomicity at type t already suffices. The atom-swapping argument extends through every relational type and fixes all closed pure terms.
database_questions.contribution: **Contribution: Lean formalization** of the Goodsell–Yli-Vakkuri theorem, following Cian Dorr’s proof sketch.

database_questions.question: Does ☐Strong Leibniz Biconditionals + Rigid Comprehension imply ☐BF at relational types?
database_questions.answer: Yes, and Strong Leibniz Biconditionals need not be boxed. The unboxed premises also imply ☐Strong Leibniz Biconditionals, ☐Rigid Comprehension and ☐Boolean Completeness. BF at type e is not claimed.
database_questions.contribution: **Contribution:** proof and Lean formalization of the stronger theorem with unboxed Strong Leibniz Biconditionals.

database_questions.question: Does Vicinity make 5-necessity imply two-hat necessity?
database_questions.answer: Yes. Sun’s argument derives the implication from a strongest 5-necessary proposition, without assuming BF or Actuality.
database_questions.contribution: **Existing database result:** Christopher Sun’s argument, with the reduction from Vicinity written out by Claude Opus 5.5 at Cian Dorr’s prompting.

database_questions.question: Can pure Maximalism coexist with Rigid Comprehension?
database_questions.answer: No. Rigid Comprehension entails Countable Boolean Completeness and hence the Necessity of Arithmetic, which is incompatible with pure Maximalism.
database_questions.contribution: **Existing result:** Zachary Goodsell, *Arithmetic is Necessary*, §6, Theorem 11 and the following remark (p. 25).

database_questions.question: Does Possible Infinity imply the corresponding Axiom of Infinity?
database_questions.answer: No, at either e or t. A singleton-individual coalesced root refutes the type-e implication; the two-object chain with a free loop refutes the type-t implication.
database_questions.contribution: **Existing countermodels:** Bacon and Dorr’s singleton-individual coalesced root; Claude Fable 5.1’s free-loop construction, prompted by Zachary Goodsell. The linked additional Infinity separations are contributions of this collection.

connections.title: Functional Choice does not give its own necessity
connections.text: The atom-plus-atomless Boolean-valued model satisfies C5 + Functional Choice + Actuality while refuting ☐Actuality and ☐Functional Choice. The two-object retract satisfies Functional Choice and ☐Actuality but refutes C5 and ☐Functional Choice.

connections.title: Substantial Choice without Plenitude
connections.text: The generic Boolean Henkin model satisfies C5, ☐Relational Choice and ☐Intensional Choice while remaining atomless and refuting Plenitude and Functional Choice at (t,t). The separate countable-support nominal model has ☐Intensional Choice and propositional Dedekind infinity while failing Relational Choice and Functional Choice.

connections.title: Intensional Choice, Relational Choice and infinity separate
connections.text: In the atom-world permutation hierarchy, ☐Intensional Choice holds at every type while operational Dedekind infinity at t necessarily fails. The paired-individual hierarchy also separates all-type Intensional Choice from Relational Choice, with the exact support-cardinal condition retained in the proof.

connections.title: What does suffice for Transversal Choice?
connections.text: Relational Choice supplies transversals for internally finite cells, and for the stated finite exceptional covers of infinite cells. ND plus matching Countable Boolean Completeness and Relational Choice suffice for internally countable cells. Admitted class labels plus Relational Choice, or an admitted well-ordered cover without Choice, give further positive cases. As all-type schemas, quotient-respecting Relational Choice is exactly Transversal Choice.

connections.title: Completeness and choice
connections.text: Directed Boolean completeness is equivalent to Boolean Completeness over C. With the matching Relational Choice instance, completeness for well-ordered chains already gives Boolean Completeness. Completeness for subfamilies of an admitted order-dense family also suffices; the countable version retains its stated countability-inheritance hypothesis. Coextension-invariant choice of comparable suprema is equivalent to Transversal, the coextension-representative principle.

connections.title: The rigidity equivalence under ND and completeness
connections.text: Over C + ND + Boolean Completeness, Inextensible Comprehension, Rigid Comprehension, Tame Rigidity and Weakly Rigid Power are equivalent. ND and Boolean Completeness alone do not imply them: the old/new model also refutes ☐Boolean Completeness at type et.
connections.contribution: **Contribution:** the rigidity equivalences and the corrected all-type Boolean Completeness verification for the existing old/new construction; both are Lean certified.

connections.title: Positive routes to Weakly Rigid Power
connections.text: Atomicity + Rigid Comprehension entails Weakly Rigid Power. ND (type t) + Inextensible Comprehension also suffices; more sharply, Inextensible Comprehension at τt gives Weakly Rigid Power at τ. These assumptions are unboxed.

connections.title: Boolean closure characterizes ND and C5
connections.text: At argument type σ, ND is equivalent to intersection, difference or symmetric-difference closure of rigid properties, and to their pointwise endpoint-valued membership; the same holds for weakly rigid properties. Complement closure is stronger: for weakly rigid σt properties it is exactly ND at σ + BF at σ, and for rigid properties exactly ND at σ + ☐BF at σ. Either all-type complement-closure schema characterizes C5; the tt test already suffices.

connections.title: Rigidity principles descend one property type
connections.text: For relational τ, each of Tame Rigidity, Rigid Power, Weakly Rigid Power, Rigid Comprehension, Weak Rigid Comprehension and Inextensible Comprehension descends from τt to τ. Their nullary instances are C-theorems. Tame Rigidity is equivalently closure of rigid relations under existing represented joins.

connections.title: Comprehension and choice do not force ☐Tame Rigidity
connections.text: One fixed-point entrance model satisfies Atomicity, Boolean Completeness, Rigid Comprehension, Relational Choice, Tame Rigidity, Rigid Power and Weakly Rigid Power, together with ☐Strong Actuality and BF at e. It refutes ☐Tame Rigidity at (tt)t, BF at every relational argument type, ND at t and Strong Leibniz Biconditionals at every relational type.

connections.title: Logical Necessity does not force Actuality or Vicinity
connections.text: For the one-predicate signature, Logical Necessity + ☐BF + ☐Relational Choice has a countermodel to both Actuality and Vicinity. A separate symmetric-surjection/free-word construction has Logical Necessity with ☐Boolean Completeness, ☐BF, ☐Tame Rigidity and ☐Weakly Rigid Power, but is atomless and fails Actuality, Vicinity and Relational Choice.

connections.title: Propositional Strong Leibniz does not give the all-type propagation theorem
connections.text: The stitched middle-world model has ☐Strong Leibniz Biconditionals at t, Rigid Comprehension, ☐BF at e and t, and ☐Relational Choice and ☐Actuality. Nevertheless ☐Rigid Comprehension and ☐Boolean Completeness fail at et. The all-relational Strong Leibniz premise in the positive theorem cannot simply be replaced by its propositional instance.

connections.title: Finite-signature SP refutes BF and Functionality
connections.text:
For every finite signature $\Sigma$, including the empty signature,

$$
\mathrm{SP}(\Sigma)\vdash\neg\mathrm{BF}_{\alpha}\;\land\;\neg\mathrm{Functionality}_{\alpha,\beta}
\qquad(\beta\ne e).
$$

This holds at every admitted input type α and relational output type β, with explicit counterpredicates and counterfunctions. With infinitely many relational constants but finitely many individual names, the type-e BF failure and input-e Functionality failures still follow. The all-input result retains the finite-signature restriction. These are consequences of SP, not a proof of its consistency.

connections.title: SP determines the finite individual domain
connections.text: With exactly u finitely many individual names, SP(Σ) forces exactly max(1,u) individuals; when u is positive the names enumerate them bijectively. Pure SP therefore forces one actual individual, refuting the individual Infinity schema and quantified Axiom of Infinity, despite its possible larger domains.

connections.title: Pure SP excludes strong worlds
connections.text: Pure SP rules out arbitrary actual strong-world entities at every relational type. It also permits distinctness-preserving atomless splitting of each fixed finite current Boolean diagram. This does not refute Actuality or weak atoms. At relational input and output types, the BF/Functionality failures can be strengthened to closed pure persistent counteroperations and arbitrarily large finite families of distinct entity-coextensive operations.

connections.title: Signature Independence is compatible with Extensionality and strong Choice
connections.text: For Σ = {c:et}, the full one-world countermodels satisfy Independence together with Extensionality and the stated Atomicity and Choice packages. They refute the proposed Infinity implications at the precise individual and propositional scopes listed in the proof.

connections.title: Quantified Infinity reduces to the base types
connections.text: Over C, Axiom of Infinity at t implies it at every relational type; Axiom of Infinity at e and t implies it at every admitted type. Under the matching Functionality instances, a relational type containing no e is internally finite exactly when t is; a type containing e is finite exactly when both e and t are.

connections.title: Infinity schemata do not imply the quantified axioms
connections.text: Even C + ☐Functional Choice has a model of both finite lower-bound Infinity schemata that necessarily refutes both quantified Axioms of Infinity. Another model has ☐Functional Choice, ☐Forcing Possibilism, ☐Axiom of Infinity at t and the individual Infinity schema while necessarily refuting Axiom of Infinity at e.

connections.title: Strong boxed structural principles do not settle CH noncontingency
connections.text: Assuming Con(ZFC), the coalesced CH model makes CH and its negation possible at the same type e while satisfying ☐Atomicity, ☐BF, ☐Strong Leibniz Biconditionals, ☐Rigid Rigidity, ☐Weakly Rigid Weak Rigidity, ☐Tame Rigidity and Modal Well-Ordering. In the full modalized cloud, the separate transfer argument realizes both CH alternatives at et.

connections.title: Maximalism refutes Non-contingency of CH
connections.text: Assuming Con(ZFC), pure Maximalism + Non-contingency of CH is inconsistent. The argument uses the separate consistency of real structures satisfying CH and its negation.

connections.title: Forcing Possibilism is independent of necessary Choice and Infinity
connections.text: Strict-smallness Forcing Possibilism is independent over C + ☐Functional Choice + Axiom of Infinity (types e and t). A free-root model also satisfies Forcing Possibilism and both quantified Infinity axioms while failing Intensional Choice. In full S5 on an infinite world set W, the exact criterion is $2^{|W|}=2^{\aleph_0}$, in external ZFC.
connections.contribution: **Contribution:** the positive model, exact full-S5 cardinal criterion and separation from Intensional Choice. The negative independence direction was already recorded.

connections.title: Choice, Plenitude and C5 through inverses
connections.text: Functional Choice is Actuality plus pointwise sections of actual surjections; Plenitude is Actuality plus pointwise retractions of actual injections. Their stronger inverse formulations distinguish ☐Functional Choice and C5. Over C + ☐Plenitude, complete Boolean retractions characterize ☐Functional Choice.

connections.title: Countable completeness at a countable Boolean type forces finiteness
connections.text: Over C, an internally countable relational Boolean type is countably complete exactly when it is internally Frege-finite. Matching Countable Boolean Completeness therefore gives Actuality in this setting. Separately, the finite-fan model has arithmetic noncollapse at e but no Possible Infinity at e, even with the stated boxed comprehension, completeness and choice principles.

connections.title: Maximalism and SP have different arithmetic obstructions
connections.text: Pure Maximalism forbids a predecessor operation at every admitted counting type, although the relevant total single-valued graph exists. Pure SP proves every standard-true Π₂ sentence under the specified Frege translation; if consistent, it omits some true Π₃ sentence. Max also refutes the explicit guarded numerical join, and its interval below ¬Actuality is internally Dedekind and Frege infinite, without asserting that ¬Actuality is currently true.

connections.title: Signature extensions and finite profile bounds
connections.text: There is an exact boundary for conservative proper extensions of finite signatures, and an infinite reserve of names restores conservativity at the types receiving new constants. Pointed complete theories determine the finite Boolean intervals forced by SP. These metatheorems retain the reference language of each Max and SP schema.

connections.title: Computational strength and model construction
connections.text: Theoremhood, finite-condition consistency and adequate model construction have distinct jump thresholds. A supplied complete consistent pure theory has a model of exactly its computational degree; requiring externally standard natural numbers creates a stronger barrier. The completion-space comparisons separate finite descriptions and effective complexity.

connections.title: Construction failures that leave the main questions open
connections.text: The rational-shear and full rational-linear selector constructions fail after the required closure steps. The paired-individual example satisfies restricted Relational Choice fragments, not full Relational Choice, so it cannot settle Relational Choice ⇒ Transversal Choice. The one-block Cohen reservoir fails the required real-uniformization property; the separate ADℝ-relative separator retains its metatheoretic assumption.

connections.title: Evaluation and coextension representatives
connections.text: The evaluator hierarchy distinguishes truth-fibre classification, correct evaluation, necessary evaluation and complete evaluation. Uniform complete-evaluator selection measures well-orderability of atom fields and, at all types, ☐Functional Choice. Coextension-invariant operations characterize Actuality at their stated type scopes.

connections.title: Logical separation and its stronger forms
connections.text: Over H, logical separation gives C + BF, endpoint separation is C5 + Atomicity at t, and factive or unique-observer separation is Extensionality. The inverse and native-modality restrictions yield further strict hierarchies. The comparison between injective and logical left-inverse separation remains open; the exact reductions and countermodel boundaries are in the observer atlas. With OS assumed over H, existence of a correct actual-truth evaluator is exactly what upgrades separation to endpoint separation. Over C, endpoint separation is equivalent to every possible world having its own unique correct evaluator, while a single evaluator that remains correct at every world is equivalent to Extensionality. See the [evaluation bridge](proofs/logical-observers.md#actual-truth-evaluation-and-endpoint-separation).

connections.title: World representations and probability
connections.text: Profile realization, complete Boolean maps and admitted world maps have exact representation theorems. Faithful probability is characterized by the stated finite-fibre numerical labelling condition, with a further countability conclusion under finite-field Choice and a finiteness obstruction at higher types.

models.name: Maximalist root
models.answer: Signature Maximalism coexists with Relational Choice and Actuality while BF (type t), Atomicity (type t) and Boolean Completeness (type t) fail.

models.name: Singleton-individual root
models.answer: Possibility⁺, Relational Choice and Actuality coexist with a singleton individual domain. The pure construction is established; its signature expansion requires at most one individual constant.

models.name: Dyadic roundings
models.answer: Actuality and Atomicity coexist with failures of BF and Boolean Completeness.

models.name: Identity-or-collapse surjections
models.answer: Actuality and BF coexist with failures of Atomicity and Boolean Completeness.

models.name: Identity-or-collapse maps
models.answer: Actuality, Tame Rigidity and Rigid Power coexist with failures of Atomicity, BF and Boolean Completeness.

models.name: Monotone maps
models.answer: Atomlessness, Tame Rigidity and Rigid Power coexist with failures of BF and Weak Inextensible Comprehension.

models.name: Monotone surjections
models.answer: Atomlessness and BF coexist with failures of ND and Weak Inextensible Comprehension.

models.name: Permutations
models.answer: ND coexists with Atomlessness and failure of Weak Inextensible Comprehension.

models.name: Truncated shifts
models.answer: Actuality, Atomicity and BF coexist with failure of Boolean Completeness.

models.name: Truncations
models.answer: Atomicity, Tame Rigidity and Rigid Power coexist with failures of Actuality and Boolean Completeness.

models.name: Two-object all-maps construction
models.answer: BF and ☐Relational Choice coexist with failures of ☐BF, Inextensible Comprehension and Countable Boolean Completeness.

models.name: Free monoid with glued constants
models.answer: Logical Necessity and Forcing Possibilism coexist with ☐Rigid Comprehension and ☐Atomicity while ND (type t) fails. The signature expansion is established.

models.name: Idempotent monoid
models.answer: ☐Atomicity and ☐Rigid Comprehension coexist with failure of Strong Leibniz Biconditionals (type t).

models.name: Involution group
models.answer: C5, ☐Atomicity, ☐BF and ☐Rigid Comprehension coexist with failure of the Fregean Axiom.

models.name: Surjection monoid
models.answer: ☐Atomicity, ☐BF and ☐Rigid Comprehension coexist with failures of ND (type t) and Forcing Possibilism.

models.name: Two-object chain
models.answer: ☐Atomicity, ☐BF and ☐Rigid Comprehension coexist with failure of pure B, and hence of No Pure Contingency.

models.name: Two-object retract
models.answer: ND, ☐Strong Actuality and ☐Rigid Comprehension coexist with failure of Strong Leibniz Biconditionals (type t).

models.name: Henkin model without a choice function
models.answer: Extensionality and Axiom of Infinity (type e) coexist with failure of Relational Choice.

models.name: Symmetric qualitative-contrast model
models.answer: C5, Actuality and Plenitude coexist with failures of Relational Choice and Atomicity. Thus Plenitude does not imply Functional Choice even under C5, Rigid Comprehension and Boolean Completeness.
